title: Prove the best-quotient staircase of the sharp net splitting tax (no κ)
body:
## Summary

For the sharp net splitting tax `N(t, σ)` of #6769, this proves where the best integer quotient switches as `σ` varies. It answers open question 2 of #6769 for every `0 < t < 1`.

Claim type: scoped written proof (Lemma 1, Theorem 2, Corollary 3 and section 5 of `PROOF.md`) plus finite enclosure certificates for five exact `t` values and `q ≤ 30`. No new κ, no supplier admission, no selected-frontier change.

```text
sigma     1 <-- tau_4     tau_3     tau_2     tau_1 --> infinity
best q          ... 4   |   3   |   2   |   1
at tau_m the best quotients are exactly m and m+1
window    zeta(m+1) < tau_m < zeta(m),   zeta(x) = (x - t W(x)) / (x - W(x))
```

- Lemma 1. For integers `1 ≤ q < q'`, the ratio `g_σ(q) / g_σ(q')` is strictly increasing in `σ`. A maximizing remainder is below 1, so the larger quotient is always paid at a larger `R = q + s`.
- Theorem 2. Each adjacent pair has exactly one tie threshold `τ_q` in the window above. The thresholds decrease to 1. Every positive integer is the unique best quotient on a nonempty open `σ` interval, so the best quotient never skips a value.
- Corollary 3. `τ_m − 1 ~ (1 − t) m^(t−1)`. At `t = 1/2`, `ζ(x) = 1 + 1/(√(4x+1) − 1)`.
- `log N(t, ·)` is convex with a convex kink at each `τ_m`.

The proof uses only facts (I1) to (I3), which `PROOF.md` quotes from #6769 and does not re-prove.

## Evidence

Before, #6769 shows the best quotient is `⌊z⌋` or `⌈z⌉` and allows ties. After, the thresholds are unique, ordered and bracketed. Certified values at `t = 1/2`, with `θ_m = z(τ_m) − m`:

| m | τ_m | θ_m |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1.6357241325 | 0.405094 |
| 2 | 1.4383632422 | 0.441590 |
| 3 | 1.3507366418 | 0.457824 |
| 5 | 1.2642332618 | 0.472944 |
| 10 | 1.1800795463 | 0.485785 |
| 20 | 1.1233222265 | 0.492734 |
| 30 | 1.0991113903 | 0.495127 |

Reproduce from the repository root with CPython 3.12.15. The exact local interpreter is `/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12`. The package uses the standard library only.

```sh
IMB_PYTHON=/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12
"$IMB_PYTHON" -I -W error -B research/net-split-quotient-staircase/verify.py
"$IMB_PYTHON" -I -O -W error -B research/net-split-quotient-staircase/verify.py
"$IMB_PYTHON" -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/net-split-quotient-staircase
"$IMB_PYTHON" -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/net-split-quotient-staircase --check-only
"$IMB_PYTHON" -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/net-split-quotient-staircase --check-source-history --check-modes
```

Local results at commit `7741b65a42e6f1bb586267afe08dc1a90d25448c`:

- Both direct runs print `PASS_NET_SPLIT_QUOTIENT_STAIRCASE`. The measured wall times are 6.74 s for normal Python and 6.38 s for optimized Python, each below its registered 300 s timeout and CI's 600 s limit. These are single executions, not benchmark estimates.
- The registered replay prints `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/net-split-quotient-staircase outcome=completed`. Both registered commands together take 13.36 s of wall time.
- The metadata check prints `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`.
- The commit check prints `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` for 6 files, source history and executable modes.

What `verify.py` checks:

- 150 enclosure-certified pairs `(t, q)` with `t` in {1/10, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, 9/10} and `q ≤ 30`. Each has a bracket of half-width at most `1e-12` around `τ_q` with `ρ_q < 1` on the left and `ρ_q > 1` on the right, the window `ζ(q+1) < τ_q < ζ(q)`, and `ζ(q+½) < τ_q`. The smallest relative margin is `3.2e-14`.
- 400 ratio evaluations on a grid, all increasing in `σ`. Also 48 envelope-slope comparisons, 12 pairs of one-sided slopes at thresholds that show the convex kink, and 261 second differences of `log N`.
- A float brute force over integer quotients 1 to 200 at 300 values of `σ` agrees with the staircase read from the thresholds.
- The `t = 1/2` closed form and `ζ(n(n+1)) = 1 + 1/(2n)` for `n ≤ 16`.
- Eight rejection controls and a nearest-integer witness. At `t = 1/2`, `σ = 1.62201395897…` has `z = 1.45`, which rounds to 1, yet quotient 2 is strictly better (`ρ_1 < 0.9925`).

## Limits

- The enclosure arithmetic widens every `exp` and `ln` result by a relative `4e-70` and treats the 100-digit rounding of `+ − × ÷` as exact. It relies on the documented correct rounding of `Decimal.exp` and `Decimal.ln`. Every certified margin is above `1e-15`, so the omitted rounding cannot change a verdict.
- The inequality `θ_m < 1/2` is certified only for the 150 pairs above. It is not proved in general.
- Lemma 1 and Theorem 2 depend on (I1) to (I3) of #6769, which are quoted and not re-proved here.
- The remark about convexity in the free exponent `u` of #6769's test (10) is conditional on `P_x` being a positive moment `Σ n_r r^x`. I did not re-read #4433 or #4480 for that form.
- `t = 1/3` and `2/3` are not exact decimals and were not certified. Nothing here covers the full split charge of #6390.
- Hosted package replay was skipped because the repository's `plan` job failed; CI certified nothing for this package. Lean and Docker were not run. No independent human or proof-kernel review is claimed.
- This is a side result on a compiler coefficient. It is not a complete multiplication theorem and says nothing about any supplier.

## Open next questions

1. Is `θ_q < 1/2` for every `0 < t < 1` and every `q ≥ 1`? What is `c_t` in `1/2 − θ_q ~ c_t / q`? The certified table has `(1/2 − θ_q) q ≈ 0.15` at `q = 30`. A first step is to prove `g(z + ½) > g(z − ½)` at fixed `σ`. The blocker is that `s_q` has no closed form.
2. For the historical #6030 application linked from #6769, does the minimizing `u` of test (10) sit at a kink `u = τ_m − t`? A first step is to scan `u` over its exact moment intervals. The blocker is those moments and the moment form of `P_x`.
3. Is `τ_m(t)` increasing in `t` for each `m`? The table suggests it. A first step is to differentiate `ρ_m(σ; t) = 1` in `t`. The blocker is the `t`-derivative of `s_q`.

The structured versions are in `TASK.json`.

## Related open work

The earlier open/merged search for "net splitting", "splitting tax", "best quotient", "quotient staircase" and "tie threshold" found no overlapping open PR, with handoff claims read up to 2026-11-10 22:26 UTC. The merged predecessor is #6769 (CubeJerry), which supplies `N` and the question. Merged #6390 covers the full split charge and its `q = 1` reduction, which this PR does not use.

The final own-account check listed all open PRs and compared those created after the CLAIM at 2026-11-10 22:15:02 UTC. The titles and bodies of #7132 (BIT stock-width fit), #7133 (dyadic aligned-window guard) and #7134 (odd-rectangle residual-rank floor) concern different objects and quantities. None requires a numerical comparison with this package.

## CI notes

At head `7741b65a42e6f1bb586267afe08dc1a90d25448c`, [run 42914936342](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42914936342) failed in the `plan` job, [job 130174850365](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42914936342/job/130174850365), at "Onboarding helper tests". The log reports 760 tests, one failure and 24 skipped. The exact failing test is `test_research_current_status.CurrentCiNavigationTests.test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record`, with ``AssertionError: '`make frontier7000-verify`' not found`` in the current section of `docs/ci-verification.md`.

The mismatch is already present at main/base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`: `certificates/selected-result.json` names `make frontier7000-verify`, while that documentation section still describes #6030 and `make frontier6030-verify`. The selected record, CI document and failing test are unchanged by this PR; its only changed paths are the six new package files.

I also read the failed job logs for [42905094314](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42905094314), [42903313790](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42903313790), [42914704054](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42914704054) (#7132), [42914729845](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42914729845) (#7133), and [42914997118](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42914997118) (#7134). Each reports the same test and missing-command assertion, with one failure among 760 tests and 24 skipped.

The package `replay` job was skipped because `plan` failed. **CI did not certify this package.** The evidence above is local verification at the exact PR head. No CI rerun or retrigger commit was made; the repository-level mismatch is left for maintainers.

## Merge danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: one new directory, `research/net-split-quotient-staircase`. No shared file, selected record or frozen source changes.
